```{python}
#| label: setup
import json
import sys

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import show

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import analysis  # constants only; the numbers come from outputs/

clusters = pd.read_parquet("outputs/clusters.parquet")
s = json.loads(open("outputs/summary.json").read())
geo = analysis.load_geojson()  # rings rewound for Plotly; see analysis.py
years = list(range(analysis.FIRST_YEAR, analysis.LAST_YEAR + 1))
last = years[-1]

latest = clusters[clusters["year"] == last]
urban_last = f"{latest.loc[latest['zone'] == 'urban', 'irca'].median():.1f}"
rural_risky = f"{(latest.loc[latest['zone'] == 'rural', 'irca'] > 35).mean():.0%}"
kept = f"{s['kept']:,}"
```

```{python}
#| label: map-setup
# One choropleth per zone. The GeoJSON is stored once per map; each year's frame
# only carries the band codes (z) and the hover values, so the file stays small.
codes = [f["properties"]["divipola"] for f in geo["features"]]
names = {f["properties"]["divipola"]: f"{f['properties']['municipio'].title()}, "
         f"{f['properties']['departamento'].title()}" for f in geo["features"]}
band_codes = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(analysis.IRCA_BANDS)}
colors = [analysis.NO_DATA_COLOR["light"]] + analysis.BAND_COLORS["light"]
labels = ["No data"] + [f"{b} ({lo:g}–{hi:g})" for b, lo, hi in
                        zip(analysis.IRCA_BANDS, [0, 5.1, 14.1, 35.1, 80.1], [5, 14, 35, 80, 100])]
n = len(colors)
scale = []
for i, c in enumerate(colors):  # stepped colour scale, one step per band
    scale += [[i / n, c], [(i + 1) / n, c]]


def band_map(zone):
    d = clusters[clusters["zone"] == zone].set_index(["year", "divipola"])

    def frame_values(year):
        irca = d.loc[year]["irca"].reindex(codes)
        z = analysis.irca_band(irca).map(band_codes).astype(float).fillna(-1)
        hover = [f"{v:.1f}" if pd.notna(v) else "no data" for v in irca]
        return z.tolist(), hover

    z, hover = frame_values(last)
    fig = go.Figure(go.Choropleth(
        geojson=geo, featureidkey="properties.divipola", locations=codes,
        z=z, customdata=hover, text=[names[c] for c in codes],
        zmin=-1.5, zmax=len(analysis.IRCA_BANDS) - 0.5, colorscale=scale,
        marker_line_width=0.3, marker_line_color=analysis.NO_DATA_EDGE["light"],
        hovertemplate="%{text}<br>IRCA (prestadores): %{customdata}<extra></extra>",
        colorbar=dict(tickvals=list(range(-1, 5)), ticktext=labels, len=0.8,
                      thickness=14)))
    fig.frames = [go.Frame(name=str(y), data=[go.Choropleth(
        z=frame_values(y)[0], customdata=frame_values(y)[1])]) for y in years]
    fig.update_geos(fitbounds="locations", visible=False)
    fig.update_layout(
        margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=10, b=85),
        sliders=[dict(active=len(years) - 1, currentvalue=dict(prefix="Year: "),
                      pad=dict(t=10), len=0.9, x=0.05,
                      steps=[dict(label=str(y), method="animate",
                                  args=[[str(y)], dict(mode="immediate",
                                        frame=dict(duration=0, redraw=True),
                                        transition=dict(duration=0))])
                             for y in years])])
    return fig
```

```{python}
#| label: pages-setup
# The Kinds, Outcomes and Method pages read the other files analysis.py wrote.
import plotly.express as px

prof = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
kind = {c: f"{c} · {n}" for c, n in prof["name"].items()}
kind_color = {kind[c]: col for c, col in prof["color"].items()}
short = {c: f"Kind {c}" for c in prof.index}          # narrow charts; colours match
short_color = {short[c]: col for c, col in prof["color"].items()}
by_year = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv")
bins = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant_bins.csv")
ksel = pd.read_csv("outputs/k_selection.csv")
legend = dict(orientation="h", x=0, y=1.02, yanchor="bottom", title_text="", entrywidth=290)
short_legend = legend | {"entrywidth": 75}


def outcome_lines(outcome, label):
    """Median outcome by year for each kind; years without data stay gaps."""
    d = by_year[by_year["outcome"] == outcome].assign(kind=lambda x: x["cluster"].map(kind))
    grid = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([list(kind.values()), years], names=["kind", "year"])
    d = d.set_index(["kind", "year"]).reindex(grid).reset_index()
    fig = px.line(d, x="year", y="median", color="kind", markers=True,
                  color_discrete_map=kind_color, custom_data=["n"],
                  labels={"median": label, "year": "", "kind": ""})
    fig.update_traces(connectgaps=False,
                      hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.1f} (n = %{customdata[0]})<extra></extra>")
    return fig.update_layout(legend=legend, margin=dict(t=40))
```

```{python}
#| title: "Kinds of municipal zone, 2016–2023"
g = clusters.groupby("cluster")
kinds = pd.DataFrame({
    "Kind": g["cluster"].first().astype(str) + " · " + g["cluster_name"].first(),
    "Zone-years": g.size().map("{:,}".format),
    "Median IRCA (prestadores)": g["irca"].median().round(1),
})
Markdown(kinds.to_markdown(index=False))
```

::: {.card title="About the map"}
IRCA is the **utility-supplied ("prestadores") IRCA** in INS open data, datos.gov.co
[`nxt2-39c3`](https://www.datos.gov.co/resource/nxt2-39c3.csv), banded by Resolución 2115
de 2007, art. 15. Pale grey: no value that year, or the zone-year was not clustered.
Boundaries: DANE [MGN 2023](https://geoportal.dane.gov.co/descargas/mgn_2023/MGN2023_MPIO_POLITICO.zip).
Descriptive only: no causal claim. Sources and caveats: `data/README.md`.
:::

## Row {height=50%}

```{python}
#| title: "Size and typical values of each kind, 2016–2023"
#| width: 62%
sizes = pd.DataFrame({
    "Kind": [kind[c] for c in prof.index],
    "Zone-years": prof["rows"].map("{:,}".format),
    "Municipalities": prof["municipalities"],
    "Urban rows (%)": (100 * prof["urban_row_share"]).round().astype(int),
    "Median IRCA (prestadores)": prof["irca_median"].round(1).astype(str)
    + " · " + prof["irca_median_band"].str.lower(),
    "Piped water (%)": prof["mean_water_coverage"].round().astype(int),
    "Poverty, 2018 (%)": prof["mean_ipm"].round().astype(int),
})
Markdown(sizes.to_markdown(index=False))
```

::: {.card title="How to read the kinds"}
k-means grouped zone-years on the nine features in the heatmap only; outcomes were never
used. A z-score is the distance from that year's mean in standard deviations: red is above
average, blue below. Names come from a fixed rule in `scripts/analysis.py`, and the risk
word is the band of the kind's median IRCA, so single zone-years can sit in other bands.
:::

```{python}
#| title: "Within each kind, IRCA vs infant mortality: Spearman ρ (municipality-years)"
#| width: 30%
d = rho.assign(kind=rho["cluster"].map(short))
fig = px.bar(d, x="spearman_rho", y="kind", color="kind", orientation="h",
             color_discrete_map=short_color, custom_data=["n"],
             labels={"spearman_rho": "Spearman ρ (−1 to 1)", "kind": ""})
fig = (fig.add_vline(x=rho["all_clusters_rho"].iloc[0], line_dash="dash",
                     annotation_text="all kinds pooled", annotation_position="top")
       .update_traces(hovertemplate="ρ = %{x:.2f} (n = %{customdata[0]:,})<extra></extra>")
       .update_xaxes(range=[-1, 1])
       .update_layout(showlegend=False, margin=dict(t=30)))
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Median infant mortality by IRCA band, within each kind"
#| width: 45%
d = bins.assign(kind=bins["cluster"].map(short))
d["irca_band"] = pd.Categorical(d["irca_band"], analysis.IRCA_BANDS, ordered=True)
fig = px.line(d.sort_values(["kind", "irca_band"]), x="irca_band", y="median",
              color="kind", markers=True, color_discrete_map=short_color, custom_data=["n"],
              labels={"irca_band": "IRCA band (prestadores)",
                      "median": "per 1,000 live births", "kind": ""})
fig = (fig.update_traces(hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.1f} (n = %{customdata[0]})<extra></extra>")
       .update_xaxes(categoryorder="array", categoryarray=analysis.IRCA_BANDS)
       .update_layout(legend=short_legend, margin=dict(t=40)))
fig
```

::: {.card title="Read with care"}
Kind 1–4 are the numbered kinds of the charts above, in the same colours.
`{python} analysis.INFANT_NOTE` Saber 11 covers 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020 and 2022.
Infant mortality and dropout are municipal; IRCA is per zone. These are descriptive
comparisons: kinds differ in many ways at once, so they do not establish causal effects of
water quality.
:::

```{python}
#| title: "Inertia by k: each extra kind must cut it by at least 10%"
fig = px.line(ksel, x="k", y="inertia", markers=True,
              labels={"inertia": "within-kind sum of squares", "k": "k"})
fig = (fig.add_vline(x=s["k"], line_dash="dash", annotation_text=f"k = {s['k']}")
       .update_layout(margin=dict(t=30)))
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Silhouette by k (higher = better separated kinds)"
fig = px.line(ksel, x="k", y="silhouette", markers=True,
              labels={"silhouette": "silhouette (−1 to 1)", "k": "k"})
fig = (fig.add_vline(x=s["k"], line_dash="dash", annotation_text=f"k = {s['k']}")
       .update_layout(margin=dict(t=30)))
fig
```

::: {.card title="Why this k"}
`{python} s["k_reason"]` Silhouette uses a fixed-seed sample of
`{python} f"{analysis.SILHOUETTE_N:,}"` zone-years. Features: IRCA, piped water and sewer
coverage, poverty, rural share, altitude, rainfall, municipal performance (MDM) and water
transfers per person.
:::

```{python}
#| title: "Search by department or municipality · clustered zone-years, 2016–2023 · infant mortality changes method in 2017"
cols = ["year", "departamento", "municipio", "zone", "cluster_name", "irca", "irca_band",
        "water_coverage", "sewer_coverage", "ipm", "infant_mortality", "saber11_mean",
        "dropout_rate"]
table = clusters[cols].rename(columns={
    "cluster_name": "kind", "irca": "IRCA (prestadores)", "irca_band": "IRCA band",
    "infant_mortality": "infant mortality (method changes in 2017)"})
table["IRCA band"] = table["IRCA band"].astype(str)
show(table.sort_values(["departamento", "municipio", "zone", "year"]), maxBytes=0,
     showIndex=False, column_filters="header", paging=True, pageLength=15,
     classes="display compact")
```
